speaker.name: Lantern
speaker.voice: Eryn – Strong Female Military Commander (ElevenLabs shared library)

rules: Spoken lines carry story and intent. They never name a key, a button, a number of credits, a stat, a range or a unit's model name: those are data that change and the on-screen card shows them from their owners (command bindings, skirmish rules, catalog).
One line per coach beat; the beat id is the coach step's id.

lines.text: Ferryman, this is Lantern. Dawn is breaking over the valley. Before anyone moves, take a good look at the ground.
Slide the map around. Get a feel for how far it runs.
Now turn the view, and tilt it. Hills hide things. Look at them from more than one side.
Pull right back and see the whole valley. Then come in close.
Those numbered flags are what this fight is about. Hold them, and the score runs our way. First side to the top wins.
This is our road in. Everything we buy arrives here. The enemy comes in from the far side.
Command has given us a budget. That's what we have to spend, and it keeps growing while the battle runs.
Open reinforcements and buy us some eyes. Scouts first.
Place them where you want them to go. Once the battle starts, they drive there from our road.
Now a rifle squad, riding in its carrier. One purchase, two units.
Nothing is on the field yet. Those are orders, not units. When the battle starts, they drive in from the road.
Start the battle when you're ready. If the clock runs out first, it starts anyway.
Here they come. Click the scouts to take command. Or use their card along the bottom.
See the treeline on the ridge? Send the scouts up there.
Good. Now face them toward the village. Drag the order out to set where they look.
Contact. Enemy outpost in the village. When you see a name in red, we can see them clearly.
Gunfire, across the river. We can't see who's shooting, but we heard it. That red patch is a contact. Something is out there.
Jump the camera to the contact. Then bring it back.
Your scouts are hidden in those trees. Keep them that way. Tell them to hold fire unless they're fired on. A scout that shoots is a scout that's seen.
The carrier's up next. Take the squad down to that stone wall by the farm.
Let them out behind the wall. Nobody fights from inside the carrier.
That farmhouse makes a fine fighting position. Put the squad inside.
There's a squad dug in at the crossroads. Put the carrier's gun on them. Keep their heads down.
They're pinned. Pinned soldiers move slowly and shoot badly. This is your moment.
Out of the farmhouse and forward. Advance, and fight as you go. Use the walls.
Hold it down and you see every order at once: the routes, where everyone ends up, and how much cover each soldier will have.
The crossroads is clear. Stand inside the ring, and the flag turns ours, as long as nobody else is in it.
Objective one is ours. Every second we hold it, the score climbs.
Enemy squad pushing back in. With both sides in the ring, it's contested, and nobody scores. Clear them out.
Armour on the north road! Enemy tank. Your carrier can't trade blows with that.
Before it gets busy: make your infantry one group, and your vehicles another. One key brings each of them back.
Pop smoke on the carrier and back out. Reverse, don't turn. Keep the thick armour toward the threat.
We have an anti-tank team in the woods, holding fire. Let the tank come to them.
Now! Order the attack on that tank.
Tank down. An ambush from cover. That's how infantry beats steel.
Our budget grows while we hold ground. Time to spend it.
Buy a supply truck, and bring it up behind the farm.
Set it up. Anything that stops nearby gets ammunition, repairs, and fresh soldiers for the ones we've lost.
Bring your battered units in. They get patched up even while they fight.
Something is hiding in that far treeline. We can't see it, but we can shell it. Buy a mortar, and fire on the ground there.
Whatever was in there won't be bothering us now.
Rotors! Enemy helicopter, coming in low.
Get air defence up, and bring it down.
Splash one. Good shooting.
Our turn. Buy a helicopter. It lifts off from our edge straight away.
Command is offering us a jet. Jets take a while to arrive. Watch its card count down.
A jet never stops. Send it in to attack, and it makes passes: in, fire, out, and around again. Mind its fuel. When it runs low, it heads home.
There's an air-defence site on that hill, and we can't see it. It's hunting our aircraft. A radar-hunting jet will find it.
There. A radar contact. We don't know exactly where it is, but we know the area. Fire into it.
Their radar's gone quiet. The sky is ours.
Ferryman, the bridge and the hill are all that's left. Take them. Your call how.
They're fighting us for that flag. While it's contested, nobody scores.
Watch the bar up top. Ours fills from the left, theirs from the right. First to the middle wins.
Every flag is ours. Total control. Outstanding work, Ferryman.
If you want a refresher on anything, the guide is in the menu. Lantern out.
Not quite. Let's run that again.
We lost one. It happens. Keep your head.
Take your time. Nothing moves until you're ready.
